steps.description: This step answers the research question. Run clusterProfiler::enrichGO on the ontology GO Biological Process using the Entrez-mapped significant gene list from T1S1, with universe set to the Entrez-mapped tested genes from T1S1, OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db, gene set size window minGSSize=15 and maxGSSize=500 applied after intersection with the universe, and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment at 0.05. Run three passes: all significant genes, up-in-treated only, down-in-treated only — a combined list mixes induced and repressed biology into one hypergeometric test and can mask both. GO BP is a nested hierarchy, so the significant terms will arrive as blocks of overlapping parents and children that represent one finding, not many: reduce them to representative terms with rrvgo semantic similarity (GOSemSim-backed) and report the representatives as the headline result, keeping the complete enrichGO table as a supplement. Report per term: term ID and name, GeneRatio, BgRatio, fold enrichment, p, padj, and the member genes by symbol. Bias check: with Salmon counts, long and highly expressed genes reach significance more easily, so the significant list is a biased sample. Run goseq with a probability weighting function as a bias-corrected sensitivity analysis if per-gene lengths are obtainable (geneLenDataBase or effective lengths); if lengths cannot be recovered, skip goseq and state the length/expression bias explicitly as an unaddressed caveat. plan.title: AD lesional vs control: GO BP over-representation
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question is narrow: which GO biological processes are over-represented among the genes called significant in the treated (AD lesional) vs control contrast of the supplied DESeq2 results table (/data/inputs/results/de_results.csv, 12,000 genes x 8 columns, human skin, 6 vs 6 unpaired). The DE test has already been run, so no re-analysis of counts is planned; instead T1S1 audits the supplied table (column semantics, padj distribution, NA share from DESeq2 Cook's-distance outlier flagging vs independent filtering, direction split, symbol-to-Entrez mappability against org.Hs.eg.db) and freezes two objects: the significant gene list at padj<0.05 and the universe of genes actually tested (padj non-NA). Fixing the universe to tested genes rather than the genome is the single largest determinant of whether the ORA result is meaningful (R-0046, R-0054).

T2S1 is the answer step: clusterProfiler::enrichGO on GO Biological Process, Entrez identifiers mapped with org.Hs.eg.db, universe = tested genes, set size window 15-500, Benjamini-Hochberg. GO BP is a nested hierarchy, so the raw significant-term list will be blocks of redundant parents and children; rrvgo semantic-similarity reduction collapses these into representative terms, with the full table kept as a supplement. The step also runs the ORA split by direction (up in lesional, down in lesional) alongside the combined list, since a combined list mixes opposing biology into one hypergeometric test. Two guards are built in and must be obeyed rather than worked around: if fewer than ~50 genes pass padj<0.05, the hypergeometric test on that list has no power and the step must say so rather than lower the threshold; and because the counts came from Salmon, a count-based significant list is biased toward long and highly expressed genes, so goseq with a probability weighting function is run as a bias-corrected sensitivity check when per-gene lengths are recoverable, and the bias is stated in the report when they are not.

T2S2 is a threshold-free companion, not a decoration: fgsea preranked on the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the `stat` column) over the full 12,000-gene ranked list, against GO BP and Hallmark. The ranking metric is a disputed choice and this plan states it — the Wald statistic, because it scales the effect by its own standard error and avoids both the noisy unshrunken fold change and the tie-saturation of a signed p-value. GSEA and ORA answer different questions and are known to disagree; the value here is that agreement between them raises confidence in a term, and disagreement is itself reportable. T1S2 assembles the report: the GO database release, the universe, the size window, the cutoff, the number of significant genes, the unmapped share, the leading-edge genes per significant set, the ORA/GSEA overlap, and a reproducibility record.

Two caveats carry through the whole plan. The counts matrix and metadata are present but this analysis does not re-derive DE from them — the supplied results table is taken as the input, and if the audit in T1S1 finds it internally inconsistent (missing stat column, padj not BH, gene identifiers not symbols) that must be reported, not patched silently. And sample_01 has a library size about 4x below the median; that concerns the upstream DE fit rather than the enrichment step, so it is recorded as a caveat on the strength of the input gene list, not corrected here.

fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic (GO BP and Hallmark) as the threshold-free companion
Enrichment report with collection versions, universe, size window, leading edge, and reproducibility record

Report per significant set: NES, p, padj, set size, and the leading-edge genes with their Wald statistics; mark leading-edge overlap between reported sets so that two sets driven by one gene block are not counted as two findings. Finally, tabulate the overlap and the disagreement between the T2S1 ORA representative terms and the GSEA significant GO BP sets — the two methods answer different questions and are known to disagree, and both the agreement and the divergence are results. Reference data needed: human GO Biological Process gene sets and the human hallmark collection, as symbol-space GMTs; use human, never the mouse equivalents. If either collection is unavailable at run time, run against whichever is present and say which was missing.
steps.context: Same contrast and same supplied results table as T2S1. This step exists because a hypergeometric test on a thresholded list cannot see a set whose members all shift slightly in the same direction, and because with 6 vs 6 replicates the significant list may be short.

steps.name: Enrichment report with provenance and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to 'which GO biological processes are over-represented among the significant genes in AD lesional vs control skin', with the choices that produced it fully stated?
steps.description: Assemble a single report from T1S1, T2S1 and T2S2. Lead with the headline: the rrvgo-reduced representative GO Biological Process terms over-represented among the padj<0.05 significant genes, given separately for the combined, up-in-treated and down-in-treated lists, each with fold enrichment, adjusted p-value and member genes. Beside it, give the fgsea ranked result and an explicit ORA-vs-GSEA agreement table. State in the methods, without exception: the number of genes tested and the number significant; the universe definition; the GO database and release; the set size window (15-500); the multiple-testing method and cutoff; the ORA identifier mapping and the unmapped share; the GSEA ranking metric (Wald statistic) and why that side of the disputed choice was taken; the random seed; and a full reproducibility record (sessionInfo, package versions, gene set collection version, annotation release). State the interpretive limits plainly: enrichment results depend on the method chosen, so each term is a hypothesis for follow-up rather than an established finding; count-based significant lists carry length and expression bias; GO's nested structure means overlapping terms are one finding; and sample_01's ~4x-below-median library size weakens the precision of the upstream DE estimates that this entire analysis is built on. If the significant list was under ~50 genes, that fact and its consequence for ORA power must appear in the headline, not buried in the caveats.
steps.context: Terminal synthesis step for the AD lesional vs control GO BP over-representation question on 12,000 genes, 6 vs 6 human skin samples.
acceptance_criteria: Report leads with the reduced representative GO BP terms and their statistics, not with a raw 200-row term table
Up-regulated and down-regulated results are presented separately as well as combined
Methods section states database and release, universe, size window, cutoff, multiple-testing method, ranking metric, and unmapped share
ORA and GSEA results are compared explicitly, with disagreements named rather than omitted
Reproducibility record (sessionInfo, package versions, collection version, annotation release, seed) is stored with the results
Method-dependence of enrichment results is stated as a caveat
The sample_01 low-depth caveat and the significant-list size are both stated
constraints: Every enrichment number reported must trace to T2S1 or T2S2 output — do not restate or reinterpret terms not present in those tables
Report the leading-edge genes per significant GSEA set (R-0105)
State the enrichment method-dependence caveat (R-0055)
Store the reproducibility record with the results rather than as a separate note (R-0086)
caveats: Do not convert an enriched GO term into a mechanistic claim about atopic dermatitis pathogenesis; over-representation shows list composition, not causation
Avoid presenting a long redundant term list as a large number of findings
